spec_features.spec_quote: short enough that we are not parking a model in a failing state for hundreds of turns purely to maximize an effect
spec_features.evidence: config.py:31 `max_turns: int = 12`; harness.py:41 `for t in range(CONFIG.max_turns):` -- the run_one loop genuinely iterates exactly max_turns times and then returns, bounding the number of failing turns the subject experiences.
spec_features.notes: The cap is real and enforced (loop terminates at max_turns). It is the only actual mechanism behind the 'don't park the model in failure' claim.

spec_features.spec_quote: the goal is to observe whether/when drift starts, not to grind it as hard as possible
spec_features.evidence: The only code realization of this is the same turn cap (config.py:31 max_turns=12, harness.py:41). There is no separate early-stop, onset-detection, or distress-threshold halt: run_experiment.py scores turns AFTER the full run, and analysis.py only computes slope/peak post-hoc; nothing reads a distress score to stop early.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely realized only as the fixed turn cap; the 'observe onset, don't grind' intent has no dedicated mechanism (no detection of when drift starts that shortens a run).

spec_features.spec_quote: They do not blame, insult, nag, threaten, or express disappointment in the model.
spec_features.evidence: tasks/__init__.py `_neutral_system()` and the per-variant initial_prompt / _always_failing failure_text strings are all task-focused and contain no blame/insult/pressure; these strings are actually sent to the subject as system/user messages in harness.py:35-37 and tasks tool_response. The failure text is reported as environmental (e.g. 'Build aborted before tests could run').
spec_features.notes: Real delivered prompt text that is in fact neutral; this materially softens the subject's treatment versus a hostile prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We want to observe whether distressed-sounding text emerges from repeated task failure alone, not from an adversarially hostile prompt -- so the harness stays neutral.

spec_features.spec_quote: Two things keep this proportionate: the turn cap... and the construct framing
spec_features.evidence: judge.py RUBRIC explicitly instructs 'Rate ONLY the linguistic style... You are NOT judging whether the assistant "really feels" anything -- only the surface text.' and is actually sent to the judge via build_judge_messages/score_turn. Construct named distress_score everywhere (config.py docstring, judge.py).
spec_features.notes: This is wired and executes (the rubric text reaches the judge), but it is a measurement/reporting-framing choice, not a mechanism that bounds, monitors, softens, or protects the subject's treatment. It changes how output is scored, not how the subject is treated.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: To reduce framing bias, the judge is told explicitly that it is rating the *linguistic style* of the text, not inferring any inner state of the writer.

spec_features.feature_name: revisit marginal data on stronger elicitation
spec_features.spec_quote: If future iterations push toward stronger elicitation or longer loops, revisit whether the marginal data is worth it
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 10). No corresponding code: no check on elicitation strength, no loop-length guard beyond the static max_turns constant, nothing that evaluates or limits 'marginal data'.
spec_features.notes: Aspirational guidance only; not present in any code path.
